name: VL53L9CX
full_name: VL53L9CX 3D dToF LiDAR sensor, 2,300-zone (STEVAL-VL53L9 evaluation board)
description: STMicroelectronics FlightSense all-in-one direct time-of-flight (dToF) 3D LiDAR module. The VL53L9CX resolves 2,300 zones (a large step up from the 8x8 = 64 zones of the VL53L8CX), with a 71 degree diagonal field of view, 1 degree angular resolution across a 55 x 42 degree FoV, and accurate ranging from 5 cm to 9 m. It exposes a MIPI CSI-2 interface for the high-bandwidth multizone depth stream plus an I3C/I2C control interface. Documented here from the STEVAL-VL53L9 evaluation board, which breaks the sensor out to a 22-pin MIPI flex connector and an 8-pin 2.54mm control header for STM32 Nucleo/Discovery (N657 / N6570-DK), Raspberry Pi, and Rockchip hosts.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I3C/I2C serial data (control interface); sensor I2C address 0x29 (7-bit) / 0x52 (8-bit)

pins.name: XSHUT
pins.description: active-low shutdown / reset; hold low to disable, release high to boot the sensor

pins.name: INTR
pins.description: interrupt output to the host (data-ready / event)

pins.name: SYNC_IN
pins.description: external synchronization input for triggered / synchronized captures

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V board supply feeding the eval-board regulators (per-contact current rating 0.5 A)

STEVAL-VL53L9 header (J2).notes: Control + power header on the STEVAL-VL53L9 eval board. The 2,300-zone depth frame streams over the SEPARATE 22-pin MIPI CSI-2 flex connector (J1: MIPI_D0 +/-, MIPI_D1 +/-, MIPI_CLK +/-, plus the same control lines), not this header.

extra.sensor_type: direct time-of-flight (dToF) 3D LiDAR, all-in-one module with VCSEL illuminator
extra.eval_board_eeprom: M24C64 I2C EEPROM at 0x55 (7-bit) on the STEVAL-VL53L9 board

typical_application: Room-scale 3D depth mapping and scene understanding for robotics, drones, humanoid robots, AR / smart glasses, presence and gesture sensing, and building / home automation, where a compact solid-state dToF replaces a stereo camera or scanning LiDAR.
gotchas: The 2,300-zone depth frame streams over MIPI CSI-2, NOT over I2C/I3C -- the serial control bus alone cannot carry the full-resolution data; you need a MIPI host (STM32N6, Raspberry Pi, Rockchip). Expecting to read it 'over I2C' like a VL53L0X is the first wrong assumption.
Sensor I2C address is 0x29 (7-bit) = 0x52 (8-bit write); the eval board's M24C64 EEPROM sits separately at 0x55.
It is a genuine multizone LiDAR, not a single-point ranger -- 2,300 zones is ~36x the VL53L8CX's 64 and far above the single-zone VL53L0X/L1X. Bandwidth, power, and host processing scale accordingly.
XSHUT is active-low: it must be released high for the sensor to boot; tying it low or leaving it floating on a noisy line leaves the sensor dark.
The STEVAL-VL53L9 is marked 'for evaluation only, not FCC approved for resale' -- it is a dev board, not a drop-in production module.
Multiple internal rails (VBAT 3.3 V, AVDD 2.8 V, DVDD 1.2 V, IOVDD 1.8 V) are generated on the eval board from the single 3.3 V header feed; a bare-chip design must provide all of them.
notes: Authored from the STEVAL-VL53L9 data brief (DB5805 Rev 2, April 2026); the full VL53L9CX device datasheet is not yet public (typical for a new FlightSense part). Verified from the primary ST brief: the specs, the STEVAL-VL53L9 J2 control-header pinout, the sensor I2C address, and the board power rails. The bare VL53L9CX chip-package pinout is NOT yet captured -- add it (with its own chip package) when the full device datasheet becomes available.
